before.title: Specified causal material response: transfer function, dispersion relations and the passivity condition
before.statement:
Assume the memory branch of the material-closure postulate [[post-em-material-closure]] in a material rest frame, and assume the hypotheses of the mathematical suppliers [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] and [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]]: Countable Choice for the smooth comparison route and, in the integrable branches, Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $E:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be the electric-field history in the material rest frame, read componentwise in its spatial basis ([[def-em-fields]]), and let $P$ be the polarisation response declared by the model.
(a) [Causal response] If the kernel of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) satisfies $K\in L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{3\times3})$, then for every bounded continuous history $E$ the response $P(t)=\varepsilon_0\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)\,ds$ is well defined for every $t$, bounded and continuous, linear in $E$, and causal: histories equal on $(-\infty,t_0]$ produce responses equal on $(-\infty,t_0]$.
(b) [Transfer function and dispersion relations] If $K$ is smooth with compact support in $(0,\infty)$, the transfer function $\chi(z)=\int_0^\infty K(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ is entire, satisfies $\chi(-\omega)=\overline{\chi(\omega)}$ for real $\omega$, obeys $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le\|K_{jk}''\|_{L^1}|z|^{-2}$ for $z\ne0$ with $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$ (with the whole-plane bound carrying the exponential factor $e^{b\max(0,-\operatorname{Im}z)}$ when $\operatorname{supp}K\subseteq(0,b)$), and its entries satisfy the principal-value dispersion relations of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]](b). If $K$ is locally absolutely continuous on $[0,\infty)$ with $K,K'\in L^1$ and $sK\in L^1$, then $\chi$ is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, continuous with continuous first derivative on the real boundary, obeys the stated growth bound, and satisfies the same pair of relations; an instantaneous real part $\chi_\infty$ may be added to the model, and the relations apply to $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}-\chi_\infty$ for $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}=\chi_\infty+\chi$.
(c) [Finitely-subtracted and polynomial branches] If the declared response transfer function satisfies the hypotheses of [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]], then the subtracted relations with the explicit Taylor polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\chi^{(j)}(\omega_0)(z-\omega_0)^j/j!$ hold for every integer $n\ge1$; the unsubtracted $n=0$ case ($P=0$, $f=\chi$, growth $O(1/|z|)$, factor $(\omega-\omega_0)^0=1$) is included. The separate constitutive-polynomial branch $\sum_{j=0}^mA_jE^{(j)}+K*E$ with real coefficients or matrices $A_j$ and $K$ as in the supplier is causal on histories with bounded continuous derivatives through order $m$, with transfer function $Q(z)+\chi_K(z)$, $Q(z)=\sum_{j=0}^mA_j(-iz)^j$; subtracting $Q$ leaves the proved relations for $\chi_K$, and $Q$ need not equal the Taylor polynomial $P$.
(d) [Monochromatic work and passivity] For $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^3$, $E(t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{-i\omega t})$ and the monochromatic response with transfer matrix $\chi(\omega)$, the period-averaged work per unit volume is $\frac{\varepsilon_0\omega}{2}\operatorname{Im}(e^*\chi(\omega)e)$; it is nonnegative for every $e$ if and only if the Hermitian dissipative part $M(\omega)=(\chi(\omega)-\chi(\omega)^*)/(2i)$ is positive semidefinite. Passivity is therefore an additional model condition, not a consequence of the causality and dispersion clauses; an instantaneous part $\chi_\infty$ contributes the storage term $\tfrac{\varepsilon_0}{2}E\cdot\chi_\infty E$ instead of irreversible averaged work.
(e) [Scope] The response is declared in the material rest frame of [[post-em-material-closure]](a); boosting the material changes the fields and the rest observer, and no frame-independent instantaneous response law is asserted. The framework does not claim that any particular material realises these branches, no microscopic mechanism is derived, and no empirical statement is made.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** identification of the declared material response with the hypotheses of the two mathematical suppliers, clause by clause, with no independent analytic re-derivation. (a)-(b): the memory-branch kernel classes of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) are literally the hypotheses of clauses (a)-(c) of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]; the identification is $P$ = macroscopic polarisation, $E$ = electric-field history in the rest frame, $\varepsilon_0$ = the framework constant of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and the transfer function is the model's polarisability matrix. Existence, boundedness, continuity, linearity, causality, the entire/holomorphic transfer function, the reality identity, the decay bounds and the principal-value relations are then those of the supplier applied entrywise; no derivative of the physical fields is taken and no additional modelling assumption is used. (c) is exactly the statement of [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]], including its $n=0$ case and its constitutive-polynomial branch; the coefficients $A_j$ are declared model data, not determined by the framework. (d) is clause (d) of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]: the period-averaged work formula and the iff-condition on $M(\omega)$. The Choice hypotheses of the suppliers are stated and carried; no stronger choice principle is used. (e) records the frame dependence and the absence of microscopic, material and empirical claims.

after.title: Specified causal material response: transfer function, dispersion relations and the passivity condition
after.statement:
Assume the memory branch of the material-closure postulate [[post-em-material-closure]] in a material rest frame, and assume the hypotheses of the mathematical suppliers [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] and [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]]: Countable Choice for the smooth comparison route and, in the integrable branches, Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $E:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be the electric-field history in the material rest frame, read componentwise in its spatial basis ([[def-em-fields]]), and let $P$ be the polarisation response declared by the model.
(a) [Causal response] If the kernel of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) satisfies $K\in L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{3\times3})$, then for every bounded continuous history $E$ the response $P(t)=\varepsilon_0\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)\,ds$ is well defined for every $t$, bounded and continuous, linear in $E$, and causal: histories equal on $(-\infty,t_0]$ produce responses equal on $(-\infty,t_0]$.
(b) [Transfer function and dispersion relations] If $K$ is smooth with compact support in $(0,\infty)$, the transfer function $\chi(z)=\int_0^\infty K(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ is entire, satisfies $\chi(-\omega)=\overline{\chi(\omega)}$ for real $\omega$, obeys $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le\|K_{jk}''\|_{L^1}|z|^{-2}$ for $z\ne0$ with $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$ (with the whole-plane bound carrying the exponential factor $e^{b\max(0,-\operatorname{Im}z)}$ when $\operatorname{supp}K\subseteq(0,b)$), and its entries satisfy the principal-value dispersion relations of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]](b). If $K$ is locally absolutely continuous on $[0,\infty)$ with $K,K'\in L^1$ and $sK\in L^1$, then $\chi$ is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, continuous with continuous first derivative on the real boundary, obeys the stated growth bound, and satisfies the same pair of relations; an instantaneous real part $\chi_\infty$ may be added to the model, and the relations apply to $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}-\chi_\infty$ for $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}=\chi_\infty+\chi$.
(c) [Finitely-subtracted and polynomial branches] For each specified integer $n\ge1$ for which the full hypotheses of [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]] hold for the declared response transfer function, its $n$-subtracted relations apply entrywise. These hypotheses include upper-half-plane holomorphy, continuity on the closed upper half-plane, the stated boundary $C^1$ regularity, holomorphy near the real subtraction point $\omega_0$, and the order-specific growth bound $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le C_{jk}(1+|z|^{n-1})$ outside a compact set. The Taylor polynomial and residual are
$$P_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\frac{\chi^{(j)}(\omega_0)}{j!}(z-\omega_0)^j,\qquad f_n(z)=\frac{\chi(z)-P_n(z)}{(z-\omega_0)^n},$$
with removable values and the boundary $C^1$ hypothesis read entrywise as in the supplier. A growth bound for one order $n_0$ permits every order $n\ge n_0$ under the same local analytic and boundary hypotheses; it does not justify lower orders for which the required growth fails. The unsubtracted $n=0$ case is included only under its own decay and boundary hypotheses: $P_0=0$, $f_0=\chi$, growth $O(1/|z|)$, and factor $(\omega-\omega_0)^0=1$ with the supplier's principal-value convention. The separate constitutive-polynomial branch $\sum_{j=0}^mA_jE^{(j)}+K*E$, with real coefficients or matrices $A_j$ and $K$ satisfying the supplier's integrable causal hypotheses, is causal on histories with bounded continuous derivatives through order $m$. Its transfer is $Q(z)+\chi_K(z)$ with $Q(z)=\sum_{j=0}^mA_j(-iz)^j$. Subtracting the declared $Q$ leaves the proved relations for $\chi_K$, without assuming that $Q$ is the Taylor polynomial $P_n$.

(d) [Monochromatic work, instantaneous work and passivity] Let $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^3$ and $E(t)=\operatorname{Re}(e e^{-i\omega t})$. Write $\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}(\omega)$ for the full transfer matrix used in the response: it is $\chi(\omega)$ without an instantaneous term and $\chi_\infty+\chi(\omega)$ when the arbitrary real instantaneous matrix $\chi_\infty\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ is present. The period-averaged work per unit volume is
$$\langle E\cdot\partial_tP\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0\omega}{2}\operatorname{Im}(e^*\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}(\omega)e).$$
It is nonnegative for every $e$ if and only if the full Hermitian dissipative part
$$M_{\mathrm{tot}}(\omega)=\frac{\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}(\omega)-\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}(\omega)^*}{2i}$$
is positive semidefinite. This frequencywise monochromatic passivity is an additional model condition, not a consequence of causality or dispersion.

For the instantaneous part set $S=(\chi_\infty+\chi_\infty^{\mathsf T})/2$ and $A=(\chi_\infty-\chi_\infty^{\mathsf T})/2$, so $S^{\mathsf T}=S$ and $A^{\mathsf T}=-A$. For any real $C^1$ history its exact instantaneous work split is
$$E\cdot\partial_t(\varepsilon_0\chi_\infty E)=\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}E\cdot S E\right)+\varepsilon_0 E\cdot A\partial_tE.$$
The symmetric part therefore supplies the quadratic storage term; no positivity of that term is asserted unless $S$ is additionally positive semidefinite. The antisymmetric part has $E\cdot A E=0$ but can supply nonzero work over a cycle. Its monochromatic contribution is $\varepsilon_0\omega\operatorname{Im}(e^*A e)/2$, and
$$M_{\mathrm{tot}}(\omega)=M_K(\omega)+A/i,\qquad M_K(\omega)=\frac{\chi(\omega)-\chi(\omega)^*}{2i}.$$
Thus only a symmetric real instantaneous matrix contributes purely this storage term for all histories; for an arbitrary real instantaneous matrix the passivity test must include its antisymmetric contribution. For example, $\chi_\infty=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\-1&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $K=0$ and $e=(1,i,0)^{\mathsf T}$ give $E=(\cos\omega t,\sin\omega t,0)$, zero quadratic storage and averaged work $\varepsilon_0\omega>0$. The opposite circular amplitude $(1,-i,0)^{\mathsf T}$ gives averaged work $-\varepsilon_0\omega$, so this instantaneous response is causal but fails the all-amplitude passivity condition.

(e) [Scope] The response is declared in the material rest frame of [[post-em-material-closure]](a); boosting the material changes the fields and the rest observer, and no frame-independent instantaneous response law is asserted. The framework does not claim that any particular material realises these branches, no microscopic mechanism is derived, and no empirical statement is made.
after.strategy:
**Proof technique:** supplier identification for the analytic branches, followed by finite-dimensional work calculations.

(a)–(b) Apply the fully stated mathematical response supplier entrywise to the declared rest-frame kernel and multiply its convolution by the framework's positive normalization $\varepsilon_0$. This retains existence, continuity, boundedness, linearity, causality, the stated entire or upper-half-plane analytic transfer, reality identity, decay and dispersion conditions. Adding any real constant matrix changes only the total transfer, and the dispersion formulas remain those for $\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}-\chi_\infty$; this analytic subtraction asserts no work or storage property.

(c) Fix an order $n$ satisfying the exact finite-subtraction supplier hypotheses. Taylor expansion near $\omega_0$ makes the zero in $\chi-P_n$ removable after division by $(z-\omega_0)^n$, and the order-specific growth yields $f_n(z)=O(1/|z|)$ in the closed upper half-plane. The supplier's boundary contour proof then gives its two principal-value relations. Do not apply it to a lower order without that order's growth bound. If the bound holds at $n_0$, then $1+|z|^{n_0-1}\le2(1+|z|^{n-1})$ for $|z|\ge1$ and $n\ge n_0$, so the growth bound also holds at every larger order. Local holomorphy near $\omega_0$ supplies all the corresponding Taylor derivatives and removable boundary regularity; away from that point division by a nonzero polynomial preserves the stated $C^1$ boundary property. The distinct $n=0$ branch requires its own decay. For the constitutive polynomial, the derivative multiplier on $e^{-i\omega t}$ is $(-i\omega)^j$, so the declared transfer polynomial is exactly $Q$, and the remainder $\chi_K$ uses the integrable supplier rather than an assumed Taylor identification.

(d) Apply clause (d) of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] to the whole monochromatic transfer matrix. Its proof uses the finite period-average identity and makes no analytic, decay, symmetry or memory-kernel assumption about that matrix, so it applies equally to $\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}$. The identity $e^*M_{\mathrm{tot}}e=\operatorname{Im}(e^*\chi_{\mathrm{tot}}e)$ proves the exact positive-semidefinite criterion. For arbitrary real $\chi_\infty$, decompose it as $S+A$. The coordinate product rule and symmetry give $\frac{d}{dt}(E^{\mathsf T}SE)=2E^{\mathsf T}S\partial_tE$, whereas $E^{\mathsf T}AE=0$ by transposition. Hence the displayed exact work split. On a periodic history the storage derivative has zero average. Because a real symmetric $S$ is Hermitian, $e^*Se$ is real; the remaining average is the stated antisymmetric quadratic form. The real matrix identity $\chi_\infty^*=\chi_\infty^{\mathsf T}$ gives $(\chi_\infty-\chi_\infty^*)/(2i)=A/i$ and the total dissipative-part formula. In the explicit skew example, $\chi_\infty e=(i,-1,0)^{\mathsf T}$ and $e^*\chi_\infty e=2i$; directly $\partial_tE=\omega(-\sin\omega t,\cos\omega t,0)$ and $\chi_\infty\partial_tE=\omega E$, giving work $\varepsilon_0\omega$ at every time. Replacing $i$ by $-i$ reverses the work. More generally, if a real antisymmetric matrix has $A_{jk}=a\ne0$, choosing $e=e_j+i e_k$ yields $e^*Ae=2ia$, hence nonzero cycle work. Therefore pure storage for all histories requires $A=0$, while $A=0$ suffices. No sign condition for an arbitrary matrix or positivity of storage is inferred from reality alone.

(e) Retain the material-rest-frame scope, every stated Choice hypothesis and the absence of microscopic or empirical conclusions. These finite-dimensional corrections add no Choice assumption and no material-realization claim.

full_object.title: Causal convolution response, transfer function and dispersion relations
full_object.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#D1-D2 (compact and W^{1,1} integrable causal branches), assembled with the passivity quadratic form
full_object.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the smooth Riemann/Lebesgue comparison route below; in clause (c), also assume Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) inherited from the AC supplier. Let $d\ge1$. All kernels below are real $d\times d$ matrix kernels and all histories are $\mathbb R^d$-valued; conditions on matrices are read entrywise, and $L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$ means entrywise Lebesgue integrability on $(0,\infty)$.

(a) (Causal convolution.) Let $K\in L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$ and let $E:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and continuous. Then for every $t\in\mathbb R$ the integral $P(t):=\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)\,ds$ converges absolutely, $$|P_j(t)|\le\sum_{k=1}^d\Bigl(\sup_{s\in\mathbb R}|E_k(s)|\Bigr)\int_0^\infty|K_{jk}(s)|\,ds\qquad(j=1,\dots,d),$$ the response $P$ is bounded and continuous, the map $E\mapsto P$ is linear, and it is causal: if $E_1,E_2$ are bounded continuous and coincide on $(-\infty,t_0]$, then their responses coincide on $(-\infty,t_0]$.

(b) (Compact branch.) If $K\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb R^{d\times d})$ (smooth, with compact support contained in the open half-line), then the transfer function $$\chi(z):=\int_0^\infty K(s)e^{izs}\,ds$$ is entire, satisfies $\chi(-\omega)=\overline{\chi(\omega)}$ for every real $\omega$, obeys $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le\|K_{jk}''\|_{L^1(0,\infty)}|z|^{-2}$ for every $z\ne0$ with $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$. For any $b>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}K\subseteq(0,b)$, the full entire-plane bound is $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le e^{b\max(0,-\operatorname{Im}z)}\|K_{jk}\prime\prime\|_1|z|^{-2}$ for every $z\ne0$. Its entries satisfy the principal-value dispersion relations $$\operatorname{Re}\chi_{jk}(\omega)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\operatorname{Im}\chi_{jk}(\xi)}{\xi-\omega}\,d\xi,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\chi_{jk}(\omega)=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\operatorname{Re}\chi_{jk}(\xi)}{\xi-\omega}\,d\xi$$ for every real $\omega$.

(c) (Integrable branch.) If instead $K:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is locally absolutely continuous entrywise in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]] on every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$, with $K\prime$ its almost-everywhere derivative with $K,K'\in L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$ and $s\mapsto sK(s)$ in $L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$, then $\chi(z):=\int_0^\infty K(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ is well defined and holomorphic on the open upper half-plane $\{\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$, continuous on the closed upper half-plane with continuous first derivative on the real boundary, satisfies the same pair of dispersion relations for every real $\omega$, and is bounded on $\{\operatorname{Im}z\ge0\}$ by $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le|K_{jk}(0)|+\|K_{jk}'\|_{L^1(0,\infty)}$ for $|z|\ge1$; for an instantaneous real response matrix $\chi_\infty\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ define $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}:=\chi_\infty+\chi$ and apply the relations to $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}-\chi_\infty=\chi$.

(d) (Monochromatic work and passivity.) Let $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^d$, and let $\varepsilon_0>0$ be a real parameter (a response normalization; the equivalence below is independent of its value). Put $E(t):=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{-i\omega t})$ and $P(t):=\operatorname{Re}(\varepsilon_0\chi(\omega)e\,e^{-i\omega t})$, real parts taken componentwise and $\chi(\omega)$ acting by matrix multiplication. Then, with $T:=2\pi/\omega$ and the Euclidean dot product on $\mathbb R^d$, $$\frac1T\int_0^T E(t)\cdot P'(t)\,dt=\frac{\varepsilon_0\omega}{2}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(e^*\chi(\omega)e\bigr),\qquad e^*\chi(\omega)e:=\sum_{j,k=1}^d\overline{e_j}\,\chi_{jk}(\omega)\,e_k,$$ and this period-averaged work is nonnegative for every $e\in\mathbb C^d$ if and only if the Hermitian dissipative part $M(\omega):=(\chi(\omega)-\chi(\omega)^*)/(2i)$ satisfies $e^*M(\omega)e\ge0$ for every $e\in\mathbb C^d$.
full_object.strategy:
Proof technique: direct, branch by branch; clausal tags below indicate the cited tools.

(a) For each $j$ and $t$, absolute convergence and the displayed bound follow from $|K_{jk}(s)E_k(t-s)|\le(\sup|E_k|)|K_{jk}(s)|$, the triangle inequality for integrals and monotonicity of the nonnegative integral over the measurable set $(0,\infty)$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]). Linearity in $E$ is linearity of the integral. Continuity in $t$: if $t_n\to t$ then $K_{jk}(s)E_k(t_n-s)\to K_{jk}(s)E_k(t-s)$ for every $s$ with the integrable dominating function $(\sup|E_k|)|K_{jk}|$, so dominated convergence gives $P(t_n)\to P(t)$ ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]). Causality: for $t\le t_0$ and every $s\ge0$ the argument $t-s$ lies in $(-\infty,t_0]$, so replacing $E$ by a history agreeing with it there changes no integrand value and hence no integral.

(b) Holomorphy is obtained from the real-parameter differentiation theorem rather than by differentiating in the complex variable directly. Writing $z=x+iy$, the integrand $K_{jk}(s)e^{izs}=K_{jk}(s)e^{ixs}e^{-ys}$ has continuous partials in $x$ and $y$; because $K_{jk}$ has compact support, on every compact set of parameters $(x,y)$ the partials are dominated by a fixed multiple of $|K_{jk}|(1+|s|)$, an integrable function, so [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign]] applied in the two real parameters gives the continuous partials $\partial_x\chi_{jk}=\int_0^\infty isK_{jk}(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ and $\partial_y\chi_{jk}=\int_0^\infty(-s)K_{jk}(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). These satisfy $\partial_y\chi_{jk}=-\int sK_{jk}e^{izs}=i\int isK_{jk}e^{izs}=i\,\partial_x\chi_{jk}$, the Cauchy--Riemann equations for the pair $(\partial_x\chi_{jk},\partial_y\chi_{jk})$ with the identification $f=u+iv$; since the partials exist on a neighbourhood and are continuous, [[thm-continuous-partials-and-cauchy-riemann-imply-holomorphic]] makes $\chi_{jk}$ holomorphic, and because the same argument is available at every $z\in\mathbb C$, each entry is entire ([[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]). Iterating gives $\chi_{jk}^{(k)}(z)=\int_0^\infty(is)^kK_{jk}(s)e^{izs}\,ds$. For the reality identity at real $\omega$: conjugation is an isometry and a real-field automorphism of $\mathbb C$ ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]) and the series defining the complex exponential converges everywhere ([[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]); conjugating the partial sums termwise and passing to the limit along the isometry gives $\overline{e^{i\omega s}}=e^{-i\omega s}$, so conjugating the defining integral of $\chi_{jk}$ and using that $K_{jk}$ is real gives $\overline{\chi_{jk}(\omega)}=\int_0^\infty K_{jk}(s)e^{-i\omega s}\,ds=\chi_{jk}(-\omega)$ ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]). On $[0,b]$, apply [[thm-integration-by-parts]] twice to the real and imaginary parts of the smooth exponential and real smooth kernel (first $K$, then $K\prime$). All derivatives are continuous and Riemann integrable; [[thm-bounded-riemann-integrable-functions-are-lebesgue-measurable-and-have-the-same-integral]] transfers each compact-interval identity to the Lebesgue integrals. With vanishing endpoint values because $K$ vanishes near $0$ and beyond $b$, these identities give $\chi_{jk}(z)=-z^{-2}\int_0^\infty K_{jk}''(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ for $z\ne0$, hence the stated upper-half-plane $|z|^{-2}$ bound; for arbitrary complex $z$, $|e^{izs}|\le e^{b\max(0,-\operatorname{Im}z)}$ on the support gives the full entire-plane bound. For the dispersion relations fix real $\omega$ and form a contour consisting of the interval $[-R,R]$ indented above $\omega$ on a clockwise semicircle of radius $\delta$, closed by the large semicircle of radius $R$ in the upper half-plane; on the indented domain the integrand $\chi_{jk}(z)/(z-\omega)$ is holomorphic, so Cauchy's theorem for null-homotopic loops gives vanishing total integral ([[cor-cauchy-theorem-for-null-homotopic-loops]]). The large arc contributes at most $\pi R\sup_{|z|=R,\operatorname{Im}z\ge0}|\chi_{jk}|/(R-|\omega|)\to0$ by the $|z|^{-2}$ bound. The small arc contributes $-i\pi\chi_{jk}(\omega)+o(1)$ as $\delta\to0$, by continuity of $\chi_{jk}$ on the closed upper half-plane, which follows from dominated convergence as in (a) ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]). The remaining real integral converges to its principal value: near $\omega$ subtract the constant $\chi_{jk}(\omega)$ so that the divided difference $[\chi_{jk}(\xi)-\chi_{jk}(\omega)]/(\xi-\omega)$ is bounded, and at infinity use the $|z|^{-2}$ decay. full_object.title: Dispersion relations for a finitely subtracted analytic response
full_object.statement: Let $n\ge1$ be an integer, let $\omega_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\chi$ be holomorphic on the upper half-plane and continuous on its closure, of class $C^1$ on its real boundary away from $\omega_0$, holomorphic on a neighbourhood of $\omega_0$ in $\mathbb C$, and satisfying $|\chi(z)|\le C(1+|z|^{n-1})$ on $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$ outside a compact set ([[def-complex-domain]]). Let $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\chi^{(j)}(\omega_0)(z-\omega_0)^j/j!$ be the Taylor polynomial at $\omega_0$ and $f(z)=[\chi(z)-P(z)]/(z-\omega_0)^n$, with the removable value at $\omega_0$. Assume the boundary restriction of $f$ is class $C^1$ (the local holomorphy supplies this at $\omega_0$). Then for real $\omega$, $$\operatorname{Re}\chi(\omega)=\operatorname{Re}P(\omega)+\frac{(\omega-\omega_0)^n}{\pi}\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\operatorname{Im}f(\xi)}{\xi-\omega}\,d\xi,$$ $$\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)=\operatorname{Im}P(\omega)-\frac{(\omega-\omega_0)^n}{\pi}\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\operatorname{Re}f(\xi)}{\xi-\omega}\,d\xi.$$ At $\omega=\omega_0$ the formula is read as the stated Taylor value. The unsubtracted $n=0$ case is also valid with $P=0$, $f=\chi$, growth $O(1/|z|)$, and the factor $(\omega-\omega_0)^0=1$ for all $\omega$; at $\omega_0$ use the same principal-value formula rather than a Taylor-value convention. For the separate constitutive polynomial branch assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), let $A_0,\ldots,A_m$ be real scalar coefficients or real matrices, and let $K$ satisfy all hypotheses of [[lem-em-integrable-causal-dispersion]]. On histories with bounded continuous derivatives through order $m$, the response $\sum_{j=0}^m A_jE^{(j)}+K*E$ is causal, and its transfer function in the $e^{-i\omega t}$ convention is $Q(z)+\chi_K(z)$ with $Q(z):=\sum_{j=0}^m A_j(-iz)^j$. Subtracting the declared polynomial $Q$ leaves the proved entrywise dispersion formulas for $\chi_K$; this branch does not require holomorphic continuation through a real subtraction point. The Taylor-subtracted formulas above apply to the total response when its additional local-holomorphy, growth and boundary hypotheses are satisfied; $Q$ need not equal its Taylor polynomial $P$. General passivity and storage remain separate model conditions.
full_object.strategy:
[[thm-taylor-expansion-holomorphic-function]] on a complex neighborhood of $\omega_0$ shows that $\chi-P$ has a zero of order at least $n$, so division gives the holomorphic removable continuation of $f$ there. Elsewhere in $H$ its denominator is nonzero. Continuity of $\chi$ on $\overline H$ and the removable continuation make $f$ continuous on $\overline H$; its real restriction is $C^1$ by hypothesis. The growth bound on $\chi$ and the degree of $P$ give $f(z)=O(1/|z|)$ uniformly in $\overline H$ at infinity. For completeness the boundary contour step is valid for any scalar $f$ holomorphic on $H:=\{\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$, continuous on $\overline H$, with $C^1$ real boundary restriction and $f(z)=O(1/|z|)$ uniformly on $\overline H$ at infinity. Fix $\omega\in\mathbb R$, $R>|\omega|+2$ and $0<\eta<1$. Use the real intervals from $\omega-R$ to $\omega-\eta$ and $\omega+\eta$ to $\omega+R$, a clockwise upper semicircle of radius $\eta$ about $\omega$, and the counterclockwise large upper semicircle of radius $R$ about $\omega$. For $\delta>0$ apply [[cor-cauchy-theorem-for-null-homotopic-loops]] to $f(z+i\delta)/(z-\omega)$ on $D_\delta:=\{\operatorname{Im}z>-\delta/2\}\setminus\{\omega-iv:v\ge0\}$. This open domain is star-shaped about any point $\omega+iA$, $A>0$, so the contour is null-homotopic there and the integrand is holomorphic. All contour pieces lie in $D_\delta$; no analytic extension of $f$ across the real boundary is assumed. On each fixed contour, continuity on a compact closed-half-plane neighborhood gives $f(z+i\delta)\to f(z)$ uniformly as $\delta\downarrow0$ by [[thm-heine-cantor-metric]], and [[thm-uniform-limit-interchanges-complex-line-integrals]] transfers the zero contour identity to $f(z)/(z-\omega)$. The large arc has $|z-\omega|=R$, $|z|\ge R-|\omega|$ and length $\pi R$, hence its contribution is $O(1/R)$. Parametrizing the clockwise small arc by $z=\omega+\eta e^{i\theta}$ with $\theta$ decreasing from $\pi$ to $0$ gives $-i\pi f(\omega)+o(1)$. Locally the divided difference $[f(\xi)-f(\omega)]/(\xi-\omega)$ is bounded because the boundary is $C^1$; the constant term cancels under the symmetric indentation. The tails are absolutely integrable by $f(\xi)/(\xi-\omega)=O(|\xi|^{-2})$. First $\eta\downarrow0$, then $R\to\infty$ therefore gives $\operatorname{PV}\int_{\mathbb R}f(\xi)/(\xi-\omega)d\xi=i\pi f(\omega)$ and the two real/imaginary formulas. Apply that boundary-contour argument to $f$, multiply both formulas by the real factor $(\omega-\omega_0)^n$, and add the complex polynomial $P$. At $\omega_0$ the factor vanishes and the removable Taylor identity gives the asserted Taylor value. The imaginary numerator subtracts the full complex $P$; it cannot be omitted.
For the distinct constitutive branch, multiplication by $(-i\omega)^j$ is the derivative multiplier on the stipulated monochromatic histories, so the transfer polynomial is exactly $Q$. Derivatives at a time are determined by a history agreeing on its whole past, including its endpoint, and the convolution is causal; hence their finite sum is causal on histories with the stated bounded continuous derivatives. The residual $\chi-Q=\chi_K$ satisfies [[lem-em-integrable-causal-dispersion]] entrywise. Without that lemma's AC and integrability conditions a merely integrable causal kernel still gives a bounded upper-half-plane holomorphic response, but does not automatically supply these principal values or Taylor continuation. The stated additional analytic assumptions, not causality alone, govern the Taylor branch.

full_object.title: Declared material-closure branches: linear nondispersive Ohmic response and the causal memory branch
full_object.statement:
Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following constitutive branches for the material described by the macroscopic fields of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]].
(a) [Material rest frame] The relations below are stated in a material rest frame: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the Minkowski model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which the material element under consideration is at rest, with spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; when the material is at rest in the laboratory frame of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the components below are the laboratory components. Boosting the material changes both the fields and the rest observer; this postulate does not assert that the relations below hold with the same constants in every frame.
(b) [Elementary inertial-rest branch] In the rest frame, with constant symmetric positive-definite matrices $\varepsilon,\mu\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ (the isotropic scalar cases $\varepsilon=\varepsilon\mathbf 1$, $\mu=\mu\mathbf 1$ with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ included), the model takes $$D=\varepsilon E,\qquad B=\mu H,\qquad J_c=\sigma E,$$ where $\sigma\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ is symmetric positive semidefinite and $J_c$ is the conduction part of the free current, $J_f=J_c+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ for a declared external free current $J_{\mathrm{ext}}$; local, linear and nondispersive (instantaneous) response is part of this restricted assumption. In the isotropic case an exact broadband interpretation of the constant-coefficient law additionally requires $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$, so that the characteristic speed $1/\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu}$ does not exceed the vacuum speed $c$; without that condition, and in the anisotropic branch, the constant-coefficient law is a declared finite-band effective phase-response model and carries no universal front-speed claim.
(c) [Causal memory branch] Alternatively, and again in the rest frame, the polarisation response to the electric history is the causal convolution $$P(t)=\varepsilon_0\int_0^\infty K(s)\,E(t-s)\,ds$$ for a declared real matrix kernel $K:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ in $L^1(0,\infty)$ ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]); the integral then converges absolutely for bounded continuous histories $E$ because $|K_{jk}(s)E_k(t-s)|\le(\sup|E_k|)|K_{jk}(s)|$. The kernel class actually used, together with causality and passivity, is part of the model and is analysed in [[pthm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]; neither causality nor passivity is automatic. A finitely-subtracted analytic response may instead be declared by a scalar transfer function $\chi$ that is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, of class $C^1$ on the real boundary away from a real subtraction point $\omega_0$, holomorphic on a neighbourhood of $\omega_0$, and satisfies $|\chi(z)|\le C(1+|z|^{n-1})$ on $\{\operatorname{Im}z\ge0\}$ outside a compact set for some integer $n\ge1$ and constant $C>0$ ([[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]).
(d) [Status] These are adopted model assumptions, one branch at a time; the framework does not derive them from the vacuum equations or from coarse graining, and no microscopic mechanism, material data or empirical validity is claimed. Ferroelectric and ferromagnetic response, hysteresis, nonlinear response and general nonlocal response lie outside the branches declared here.

full_object.title: Energy balance and Ohmic dissipation for the constant nondispersive linear model
full_object.statement:
Assume the elementary inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]]: constant symmetric positive-definite matrices $\varepsilon,\mu\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ (isotropic scalar case included) with $D=\varepsilon E$ and $B=\mu H$, and the conduction relation $J_f=\sigma E+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ with $\sigma$ symmetric positive semidefinite and a declared external free current $J_{\mathrm{ext}}$. Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with the regularity hypotheses of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], so that its macroscopic equations hold on $\Omega\times I$. Define the stored-energy density and the energy-flux vector $$u:=\tfrac12\bigl(E\cdot D+B\cdot H\bigr),\qquad S:=E\times H,$$ with the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; $u$ carries $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$ and $S$ carries $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Then:
(a) [Local balance and positivity] On $\Omega\times I$, $$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J_f\cdot E.$$ Moreover $u=\tfrac12(E\cdot\varepsilon E+H\cdot\mu H)\ge0$, with $u(x,t)>0$ whenever $(E(x,t),H(x,t))\ne(0,0)$.
(b) [Dissipation reading] With $J_f=\sigma E+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\sigma$ symmetric positive semidefinite, $E\cdot\sigma E\ge0$ and the balance reads $$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S+E\cdot\sigma E=-J_{\mathrm{ext}}\cdot E;$$ the nonnegative term $E\cdot\sigma E$ is the Ohmic dissipation density of the model.
(c) [Fixed-volume balance] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with $\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let $t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) as in that divergence theorem, and let $n$ be the outward unit normal of $\partial\Omega'$. Then for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$, $$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}u(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\Omega'}J_f\cdot E\,dx-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}S\cdot n\,dS.$$
(d) [Scope] The density $u=\tfrac12(E\cdot D+B\cdot H)$ is a stored-energy density only for this constant symmetric nondispersive model; for general dispersive, nonlocal, nonlinear or hysteretic response no instantaneous stored-energy density is defined or claimed by this item, and the general dispersive work balance is not supplied. The identities hold only where the fields and sources have the stated regularity, the fixed-volume form keeps its boundary term, and no conservation of $\int_{\Omega'}u$ is asserted unless that term vanishes. No empirical claim is made.
full_object.strategy: **Proof technique:** dot the macroscopic curl equations with the complementary fields and use the cross-product divergence identity. (a): by [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], $\operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. Taking the Euclidean inner product ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) of the first with $E$ and of the second with $H$ gives $E\cdot\operatorname{curl}H=E\cdot J_f+E\cdot\partial_tD$ and $H\cdot\operatorname{curl}E=-H\cdot\partial_tB$. By [[lem-the-divergence-and-curl-of-a-cross-product]], $\operatorname{div}(E\times H)=H\cdot\operatorname{curl}E-E\cdot\operatorname{curl}H$; subtracting the two scalar equations from this identity gives $\operatorname{div}S+\partial_t\bigl(\tfrac12E\cdot D+\tfrac12B\cdot H\bigr)+J_f\cdot E=0$, because the symmetry of $\varepsilon$ gives $E\cdot\partial_tD=\tfrac12\partial_t(E\cdot\varepsilon E)$ and the symmetry of $\mu$ gives $H\cdot\partial_tB=\tfrac12\partial_t(H\cdot\mu H)$, using $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ and the product rule of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. Positivity is positive definiteness of $\varepsilon,\mu$: $u$ is a sum of two nonnegative quadratic forms, vanishing only when $E=H=0$. (b): $J_f\cdot E=E\cdot\sigma E+J_{\mathrm{ext}}\cdot E$ and $E\cdot\sigma E\ge0$ for symmetric positive semidefinite $\sigma$. (c): [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates $t\mapsto\int_{\Omega'}u$ under the integral sign and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] converts $\int_{\Omega'}\operatorname{div}S$ into the boundary flux; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly the hypothesis of that divergence theorem and is used only in this clause. (d) records the restrictions. No constitutive assumption beyond the declared closure branch, and no empirical premise, is used.

full_object.title: Matching units does not determine the permittivity or the response law
full_object.statement:
(a) [Dimensional exclusion of $E=\varepsilon_0D$] In the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: the electric constant $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ carries $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm C^2\mathrm s^2\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-3}$, the displacement $D$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and the electric field $E$ of [[def-em-fields]] carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$. The product $\varepsilon_0D$ therefore carries $\mathrm F\,\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm C^3\mathrm s^2\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-5}$, which is not the dimension of $E$: the proposed identification $E=\varepsilon_0D$ fails dimensionally in SI and cannot be a field relation of the framework.
(b) [Units do not determine the law] Solving the definition $D=\varepsilon_0E+P$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] gives $E=(D-P)/\varepsilon_0$, which in vacuum ($P=0$) reads $E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}D$. Any proposed law $E=\eta D$ with a constant $\eta>0$ of dimension $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm C^{-1}$ is dimensionally admissible; dimensional consistency therefore does not identify $\eta$, and it does not determine whether the response is local, linear or instantaneous. In the model of [[post-em-material-closure]] the scalar relation is $D=\varepsilon E$, i.e. $\eta=\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ (or $\chi_e=\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0-1$) is fixed by the declared material model, not by units.
(c) [Frequency-domain symbols are not instantaneous coefficients] In the memory branch of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) the response is a causal convolution in time; a scalar $\varepsilon(\omega)$ introduced in the harmonic description acts on the Fourier components of the field history in the material rest frame. The framework therefore does not read $\varepsilon(\omega)$ as an instantaneous multiplicative coefficient in the time domain: doing so silently replaces the convolution by an instantaneous law and is a model-identification error of the same kind as (a).
(d) [Scope] A dimensional and model-identification statement about the framework's own conventions; it asserts no measurement, no material property and no empirical claim.
full_object.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct dimensional computation and immediate consequences of the definitions. (a): the units of $\varepsilon_0$, $D$ and $E$ are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the derived-unit identities $\mathrm F=\mathrm C\,\mathrm V^{-1}$ and $\mathrm V=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^2\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$ give $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm C^2\mathrm s^2\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$; multiplying the first by $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ gives $\mathrm F\,\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, a different combination of the base units $\mathrm{kg},\mathrm m,\mathrm s,\mathrm C$. (b): $D=\varepsilon_0E+P$ is a definition of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]], and solving it is elementary algebra; the vacuum constant $\eta=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ has the dimension of $E/D$ while being a model constant. (c): the memory branch is a convolution in time by [[post-em-material-closure]](c); a harmonic symbol acts on Fourier components and does not define an instantaneous coefficient. No physical measurement and no particular material is asserted.

full_object.title: Hypothesis boundaries: a causal response without passivity, and the fixed-retarded-time flux limit
full_object.reference: mathematical-example-verifications.md#ex-em-causal-response-and-radiation-prerequisites-hypothesis-boundaries; clause (ii) added by this scaffolder to exercise the second theorem's declared dependency (recorded in the batch notes)
full_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the surface-integral conventions used by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]].

(i) (Causality without passivity.) In this clause also assume Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the exact AC supplier. Let $K(s):=-e^{-s}$ for $s\ge0$. Then $K$ is of class $C^1$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $K,K'\in L^1(0,\infty)$ and $sK(s)\in L^1(0,\infty)$ (indeed $K'=e^{-s}=-K$, $\int_0^\infty e^{-s}ds=1$ and $\int_0^\infty se^{-s}ds=1$), so the integrable branch of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] applies: $P(t)=\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)ds$ is a bounded causal linear response on bounded continuous histories, its transfer function is $\chi(z)=-1/(1-iz)$ on $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$, and its boundary value $\chi(\omega)=-(1+i\omega)/(1+\omega^2)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)=-\omega/(1+\omega^2)<0$ for every $\omega>0$. Hence the Hermitian dissipative part $M(\omega)=\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)$ is strictly negative, not positive semidefinite, and the monochromatic period-averaged work of clause (d) of that theorem is strictly negative for $d=1$, every $e\ne0$ and every $\omega>0$ (with any response normalization $\varepsilon_0>0$), although the response is causal and its entry satisfies the dispersion relations of clause (c). Nonnegative period-averaged work (passivity) is therefore an additional condition on the model, not a consequence of temporal causality.

(ii) (The flux limit needs fixed retarded time.) In the setting of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]], fix $t\in\mathbb R$ and $n\in S^2$, and let $r>\max\{2a,\;a+c(t-t_0)\}$. Then for every $y\in B_a$ one has $R=|rn-y|\ge r-a>c(t-t_0)$, so $t-R/c<t_0$; by hypothesis (H1) of that theorem the functions $\rho,\rho_t,\mathbf J,\mathbf J_t$ all vanish at $(y,t-R/c)$, so every integrand in the field formulas of clause (a) of that theorem vanishes and $\mathbf E(rn,t)=\mathbf B(rn,t)=0$, hence $n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)=0$ for every $n\in S^2$. Therefore $\int_{S^2}r^2\,n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)\,d\Omega(n)=0$ for all such $r$: at fixed observation time the far-zone flux integral is identically zero beyond the light cone of the compact spacetime support, whereas clause (c) of that theorem is a limit at fixed retarded time. The retarded-time formulation cannot be replaced by a fixed-observation-time one.
full_object.strategy:
Proof technique: direct computation and direct substitution into the two cited theorems.

(i) The real exponential is differentiable with $\exp'=\exp$ ([[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]) and $\exp(-s)>0$ with $\exp(-s)=1/\exp(s)$ ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]), so $s\mapsto K(s)=-e^{-s}$ is of class $C^1$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $K'=e^{-s}=-K$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). For every $N>0$ the Newton-Leibniz formula gives $\int_0^Ne^{-s}ds=1-e^{-N}$ and integration by parts (with $u=s$, $v=-e^{-s}$) gives $\int_0^Nse^{-s}ds=1-(1+N)e^{-N}$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-integration-by-parts]]); the continuous real integrands have the same Lebesgue integrals by [[thm-bounded-riemann-integrable-functions-are-lebesgue-measurable-and-have-the-same-integral]]; [[thm-c1-lipschitz-ac-bv-hierarchy]] proves the explicit $C^1$ kernel is absolutely continuous on each compact interval in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]; the displayed Newton-Leibniz integral representations agree with the Lebesgue FTC under this regularity. Thus it has the absolute-continuity property required by the integrable branch of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]], and passing to the limit with monotone convergence for the nonnegative integrands gives $\int_0^\infty e^{-s}ds=\int_0^\infty se^{-s}ds=1$, so $K,K',sK(s)\in L^1(0,\infty)$ ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]). Clause (a) of the theorem therefore gives the bounded causal response. For the transfer function, fix real $\omega$; the complex exponential is entire with derivative itself and the complex chain rule gives that $s\mapsto F(s)=\exp((-1+i\omega)s)/(-1+i\omega)$ is a primitive of $s\mapsto\exp((-1+i\omega)s)$ on $\mathbb C$ ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-complex-derivatives]], [[def-complex-exponential]]), so the fundamental theorem for complex line integrals along the interval path $[0,N]\ni s\mapsto s$ gives $\int_{[0,N]}\exp((-1+i\omega)s)\,ds=F(N)-F(0)$ ([[thm-fundamental-theorem-for-complex-line-integrals]], [[def-complex-primitive]], [[def-complex-line-integral-over-a-rectifiable-path]], [[thm-riemann-stieltjes-and-parametric-contour-integrals-agree]]). Hence $\int_0^N(-e^{-s})e^{i\omega s}ds=-(F(N)-F(0))$, and $\left|e^{(-1+i\omega)N}\right|=e^{-N}\to0$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); letting $N\to\infty$ with dominated convergence for the integrands dominated by $e^{-s}$ gives $\chi(\omega)=-1/(1-i\omega)$, and the same computation with $z$ in place of $\omega$ gives $\chi(z)=-1/(1-iz)$ for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$ ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]). Taking real and imaginary parts ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) gives $\chi(\omega)=-(1+i\omega)/(1+\omega^2)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)=-\omega/(1+\omega^2)<0$ because $\omega>0$. With $d=1$, $e=1$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$, clause (d) of the theorem gives period-averaged work $\frac{\varepsilon_0\omega}{2}\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)<0$ and $M(\omega)=\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)<0$, so the passivity condition fails while causality holds: this witnesses the logical independence recorded in the theorem's proof discussion.

(ii) For $y\in B_a$ the reverse triangle inequality gives $R=|rn-y|\ge r-a>c(t-t_0)$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), hence $t-R/c<t_0$ and all four source functions vanish at the arguments appearing in the field integrals of clause (a) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]; each integrand is identically zero on $B_a$, so $\mathbf E(rn,t)=\mathbf B(rn,t)=0$ and therefore $n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)=\mu_0^{-1}n\cdot(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)(rn,t)=0$ for every $n\in S^2$. The surface integral of the zero function vanishes ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), so the fixed-observation-time flux integral is $0$ for every $r>\max\{2a,a+c(t-t_0)\}$, while the limit displayed in clause (c) of that theorem is taken with $u$ fixed and $r\to\infty$ along $t=u+r/c$; the two formulations therefore differ and the retarded-time one is essential.
